rivals.name: open licence
rivals.match: released under an open licence, without exception

wordings.text: Everything made in the residency is released under an open licence, unless a majority of residents agree an exception.
wordings.why: Without exception is a promise we will break the first time somebody builds something for a vulnerable user group.

wordings.text: Code is open by default; everything else is the maker's own.
wordings.why: Open source is a software norm. Forcing it onto essays, research and designs is a category error.

wordings.text: Nothing made here need be released at all. The residency is a place to work, not a licence.
wordings.why: People do their best work when nobody owns the output but them.

wordings.text: Everything made in the residency is released under a copyleft licence, so that what is built on it stays open too.
wordings.why: A permissive licence is a gift to whoever encloses it next.

wordings.text: Work is released openly once the resident leaves, and not before.
wordings.why: Half-made things released early get judged as finished things.

wordings.text: Anything paid for with the residency's money is open; anything paid for by the resident is theirs.
wordings.why: The obligation should follow the money, not the postcode.

wordings.text: Everything made in the residency is published, in whatever state it is in, on the day the residency ends.
wordings.why: A deadline is the only thing that makes people publish.

wordings.text: Residents decide for themselves what to release, and say in public what they have chosen not to.
wordings.why: Transparency about the choice matters more than the choice.

wordings.text: Everything made in the residency is released under an open licence, and the residency may also license it commercially to fund itself.
wordings.why: Dual licensing is how open projects pay their rent.

wordings.text: Open is the default; a resident may keep a project closed by telling the house why, in writing, and the reason is published.
wordings.why: A default with a public opt-out gets nearly everything open without making liars of us.

wordings.text: Everything made in the residency belongs to the residency, which releases it openly.
wordings.why: If the house is the owner, nobody can quietly close it later.

wordings.text: Everything made in the residency is released into the public domain, without exception.
wordings.why: A licence is still a claim. Give it away properly.

rivals.name: AI tools
rivals.match: Residents may use AI tools to draft, research and code, but every published word is read by a person

wordings.text: Residents may use AI tools however they like; what matters is what they ship.
wordings.why: We do not regulate which text editor people use either.

wordings.text: No text or code produced by an AI is published under the residency's name.
wordings.why: The residency's name should mean a person thought this.

wordings.text: Residents may use AI tools to draft, research and code, and must say so wherever they have.
wordings.why: Disclosure, not prohibition. Readers can decide what it is worth.

wordings.text: AI tools may draft, but may not be given the residency's data, its members' names, or anything said in the house.
wordings.why: The risk is not what comes out of the model, it is what goes in.

wordings.text: Residents are expected to use AI tools; the residency exists to find out what political technology looks like when they are.
wordings.why: A political technology institution that is cautious about the defining technology of the decade has missed its own point.

wordings.text: Residents may use AI to write code, and not prose.
wordings.why: Code is tested by running it. Prose is tested by trusting the author.

wordings.text: Whatever an AI writes is the resident's own responsibility, exactly as if they had written it by hand.
wordings.why: One rule: you sign it, you own it. Everything else follows.

wordings.text: AI tools may draft, research and code; they may not vote, decide, or speak for a resident in any decision of the house.
wordings.why: Drafting is labour. Deciding is membership.

wordings.text: Residents may use AI tools to research and code, but every published word is written by a person.
wordings.why: Read by a person is a rubber stamp. Written by a person is a standard.

wordings.text: Residents keep a public log of every AI tool they use and what they use it for.
wordings.why: We should be the place that has the data on how this work is really done.

wordings.text: The residency runs its own models on its own machines; nothing goes to a vendor.
wordings.why: An institution about power should not rent its thinking from five companies.

rivals.name: money
rivals.match: takes no money from political parties, and none from any government\.

wordings.text: The residency takes money from anyone, and publishes every donor's name and amount.
wordings.why: Purity is a luxury; disclosure is the actual safeguard.

wordings.text: The residency takes no money from political parties; government grants are accepted and published.
wordings.why: Most civic technology is government-funded. Refusing it means refusing to exist.

wordings.text: The residency takes no money from political parties, from governments, or from any company whose business is politics.
wordings.why: The lobbyists and the consultancies are the gap in the current wording.

wordings.text: The residency is funded by its residents' fees and nothing else.
wordings.why: Whoever pays, owns. It should be us.

wordings.text: The residency takes no money from political parties, and no gift from any one source above a tenth of its income.
wordings.why: Dependence is the danger, not the donor's identity.

wordings.text: The residency takes no money from anybody who asks for anything in return.
wordings.why: The test is the string, not the source.

wordings.text: The residency takes money from anyone, but no funder may name a resident, set a project, or see anything before it is published.
wordings.why: Wall the money off from the work and it does not matter whose it is.

wordings.text: The residency takes no money from political parties or governments, nor any gift the residents have not voted to accept.
wordings.why: The people whose reputations are spent should be the ones who decide.

wordings.text: The residency takes no money from political parties, or from any government but our own.
wordings.why: Foreign state money in political technology is a different thing from an Arts Council grant.

wordings.text: Funding decisions are the director's alone, and the residents are told afterwards.
wordings.why: A committee has never once raised money.

wordings.text: The residency takes no money from political parties, none from any government, and none from any company.
wordings.why: If a party's money compromises us, a platform company's certainly does.
